title: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt
hook: a blacksmith who suffered for his faith in Mecca, and lived to see the community grow

segments.voice: Yesterday: Suhayb, who handed over his wealth at a roadblock and was told he had profited. Your line was a profitable trade.

I won't pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. A man in Mecca says that to the craftsman he owes. The craftsman is a blacksmith named Khabbab, come to collect for work already done. The man who owes him is al-As ibn Wa'il. The bill is real: the work is done, and the money is owed. The price he puts on paying it is Khabbab's faith. Today: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, the blacksmith.
screen: `AN ANVIL AND A FIRE.` → `AN UNPAID BILL.` → `A PRICE FOR HIS FAITH.`

segments.voice: That scene is Khabbab's own telling, in Sahih al-Bukhari. He answered al-As that he would not disbelieve, not until al-As died and was raised again. Bukhari connects verses in surah nineteen to that exchange. Tradition says Khabbab paid for his faith with his body too, that he was made to lie on hot coals, and that years later he showed the scars on his back. The texts keep something quieter as well. In another report in Bukhari, Khabbab remembers going to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, who was resting on his cloak in the shade of the Kaaba. Won't you ask God to help us? The Prophet sat up. He spoke of believers before them who had suffered terribly and still not turned from their faith. Then he said God would complete this matter, until a rider could travel from San'a to Hadramawt fearing no one but God, and the wolf for his sheep. But you are in a hurry, he said. That's a hard answer to hear when you are the one hurting. It doesn't deny the pain. It widens the frame. And Khabbab lived to see the frame widen. A third report in Bukhari has him, much later, remembering the companions who emigrated. Some died before tasting any reward, he says, and he names Mus'ab ibn Umayr, whom we have met on this road. And some of us, Khabbab says, have seen our fruit ripen, and we are picking it. In his own reports, what he holds on to is not that the fire was small, but the wider frame the Prophet showed him.
screen: `NOT UNTIL YOU DIE AND RISE AGAIN.` · `WON'T YOU ASK GOD TO HELP US?` · `A RIDER WHO FEARS NO ONE BUT GOD.` · `OUR FRUIT HAS RIPENED.` · then, large: `THE BLACKSMITH ENDURED.`

segments.voice: This week ran from Rufaydah's tent, through al-Shifa, Umm Sulaym, Hassan, Ka'b and Suhayb, to Khabbab. Sit up a little straighter than is easy, and stay there; it isn't suffering, just a small chosen effort, and you can let it stand for someone you're helping or something you're building. If you pray, you can ask God for patience.
Khabbab. The blacksmith of Mecca who would not give up his faith for an unpaid debt, and lived to see the fruit ripen. Today's word.
Your line: the blacksmith endured. He lived to see the fruit ripen. That's day eight hundred fifty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims tell Khabbab's story from his own reports in Sahih al-Bukhari, where he speaks of his trade, of asking the Prophet for help in Mecca, and of the companions who did and did not live to see the community grow.

chat.says: When Khabbab asked the Prophet to pray for help in Mecca, what did he hear?
options: That God would complete this matter, but you are in a hurry.
That the persecution would end within the year, by a miracle.
That suffering meant God was angry with the believers.
chat.meaning: In Bukhari, the Prophet spoke of believers before them who endured, said God would complete this matter, and added: but you are in a hurry.

Khabbab ibn al-Aratt.meaning: a blacksmith of Mecca who kept his faith

al-As ibn Wa'il.meaning: the Meccan who owed Khabbab money

Kaaba.meaning: the house of worship at the center of Mecca

Mus'ab ibn Umayr.meaning: a companion who died before tasting any reward

notes: Week-end day (848–854): the practice names the week.
The hot coals and the scars on his back are framed as 'tradition says' (they come from later biographical works, e.g. Ibn Sa'd), not the cited hadith; confirm.
Bukhari 3612's description of earlier believers' tortures is summarized gently ('suffered terribly'), not detailed.
Hadith numbers (Bukhari 2091, 3612, 1276) cited from memory; confirm. Confirm that the verses linked are 19:77–80.
The teaser hook was softened from the index ('tortured on hot coals') to keep the coals as tradition; owner may prefer the index wording.
'A sword half finished' in the hook: some versions of the report say Khabbab had made a sword for al-As; confirm, or cut to 'a blade'.
